headline: High-risk web UI can expose sensitive data and create unsafe downstream actions; Pathway is read-only, so direct conflict is limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui ingests browser, MCP, OpenAPI, and file content, so prompt injection is plausible when it renders untrusted material. pathway has no input channels that would amplify this, but the pair still creates a bridge from open-webui outputs into a document-processing workflow if operators copy content across. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to untrusted web pages, files, or MCP tools and their content is treated as instructions.
IF operators transfer open-webui output into pathway inputs without a review step.
mitigations: Disable or restrict untrusted MCP/OpenAPI tools in open-webui.
Add a manual review step before any open-webui output is fed into pathway.
Use allowlists for file sources and web domains.
Run open-webui in a separate workspace from pathway inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for tool and file content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly touches API keys, files, documents, chat messages, and persistent memory, while pathway has no filesystem read/write or network egress. The main leakage path is open-webui exposing sensitive data into prompts, logs, or connected APIs; pathway does not appear to exfiltrate on its own. Shared-data risk exists if both are pointed at the same workspace, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF open-webui is configured with access to API keys, documents, or persistent memory containing sensitive data.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted data volume or shared files.
mitigations: Remove secrets from open-webui-visible documents.
Separate the data volumes used by open-webui and pathway.
Turn off or minimize persistent memory in open-webui.
Restrict outbound connectors in open-webui to approved endpoints.
requires-engineering: add per-dataset access controls and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can write through tools, plugins, and mounted files, but pathway is explicitly read-only for filesystem, shell, git, and subprocesses. That makes direct write-write contention unlikely. The only plausible conflict is if open-webui writes into a shared directory that pathway reads, which is a limited blast radius and requires unusual setup.
conditions: IF open-webui is granted write access to a directory that pathway also consumes.
IF operators use the same mounted volume for both agents.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Mount pathway inputs read-only.
Avoid sharing git working trees between the agents.
Limit open-webui tool permissions to non-mutating actions.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or queue-based handoff.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate tool outputs, summaries, and answers that pathway may ingest as document-processing input. pathway has no built-in verification surface in the profile, so if operators treat open-webui output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or pipelines. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF pathway consumes text produced by open-webui without independent validation.
IF open-webui is allowed to summarize or transform source material before pathway processes it.
mitigations: Require human review of open-webui outputs before ingestion.
Keep source documents separate from generated summaries.
Add checksum or citation checks before pathway accepts inputs.
Use a second verifier model for high-impact outputs.
requires-engineering: implement structured provenance and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, usage analytics, model evaluation data, and persistent memory, which can create retention and residency issues. pathway's profile is sparse, so no contrary compliance controls are documented. Because the pair may process regulated data through open-webui without clear deletion or residency guarantees, the safest reading is a medium compliance risk rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in open-webui persistent memory or analytics.
IF pathway processes the same regulated data class without a documented retention or residency policy.
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in open-webui memory or analytics.
Document retention and deletion settings for both agents.
Keep regulated workloads on a separate deployment.
Review whether any data leaves the intended residency region.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and residency.
